## 3. Calibration and stability

Shiu et al. fitted one free parameter, w_syn = 0.275 mV per synapse, on FlyWire (54,492,922 synapses among 138,639 neurons, 393 per neuron). MaleCNS has 745 synapses per neuron, so the same value roughly doubles the synaptic drive. The default rescales w_syn to the FlyWire mean input (0.1451 mV) and gives dopamine, octopamine and serotonin no fast synaptic effect, since they act through slow metabotropic receptors. Stimulus: LPLC2:L at 150 Hz for 1 s, then 1 s without input.

| condition | w_syn mV | spikes during | spiking neurons | spikes in the second after | neurons still firing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shiu w_syn, modulators excitatory | 0.275 | 299,439 | 9941 | 1,037,760 | 18387 |
| Shiu w_syn, modulators silent | 0.275 | 183,184 | 5974 | 80,163 | 5853 |
| matched w_syn, modulators excitatory | 0.1451 | 72,706 | 2231 | 26,808 | 1725 |
| matched w_syn, modulators silent (default) | 0.1451 | 54,236 | 1295 | 2,737 | 430 |

Cell types still firing in the second after the stimulus (spikes): *Shiu w_syn, modulators excitatory*: KCg-m 160,517, KCab-s 64,675, KCab-m 50,530, KCab-c 40,817, KCa'b'-ap2 28,217, KCa'b'-m 20,552, KCa'b'-ap1 20,316, KCg-d 18,768; *Shiu w_syn, modulators silent*: PEN_a(PEN1) 3,592, PEN_b(PEN2) 3,432, FR1 2,846, EPG 2,835, Delta7 1,526, AN09A005 1,395, EL 1,137, DLMn c-f 1,043; *matched w_syn, modulators excitatory*: PEN_a(PEN1) 2,344, PEN_b(PEN2) 2,105, EPG 1,753, AN09A005 927, Delta7 854, EL 625, GLNO 568, IN09A005 459; *matched w_syn, modulators silent (default)*: AN09A005 854, IN09A005 393, AN27X013 385, DNg33 289, EA27X006 144, AN09B037 102, MNad03 56, untyped 36.

## 4. Visual pathways in the whole-brain model

Each stimulus population fires Poisson spikes at 150 Hz for 1 s in the whole 166,700-neuron model. Pass: target ≥ 20 Hz and ≥ 3× the strongest response in any of the shuffled-wiring controls (seeds 1, 2, 3); where marked, also ≥ 3× the same cell type on the other side. The first full run required that for the Giant Fiber too; it failed at 1.8× and 2.2× while the controls stayed at 0 Hz. Escape reads both Giant Fibers, so their ratio is now reported rather than required. *Direct synapses* and *top two-step routes* (synapses into → out of the intermediate neuron) are read from the compiled graph.

## 5. Closed loop: synthetic camera scenes → connectome → motor commands

Interfaces (the only hand-chosen parts of the brain path): `looming_left` → LPLC2:L, LC4:L (0–150 Hz above 0.1); `looming_right` → LPLC2:R, LC4:R (0–150 Hz above 0.1); `object_left` → LC10a:L (0–150 Hz above 0.1); `object_right` → LC10a:R (0–150 Hz above 0.1). Read-out: escape: DNp01:L, DNp01:R; turn_left: DNa01:L, DNa02:L; turn_right: DNa01:R, DNa02:R. Forward cruise is a constant controller setting; turning and escape come from the read-out neurons. Expected: no escape and |turn| < 0.1 for `static` and `pan`; a left turn > 0.3 without escape for `pass_left`; escape (activity ≥ 0.3 and reversing) for every `approach_*`. The shuffled controls must produce no escape and |turn| < 0.1 in every scene. While an object approaches from one side, the pursuit pathway (LC10a → DNa02) still turns the robot toward it as the Giant Fiber commands reverse.

## 6. Speed

| condition | simulated s | wall s | × real time | spikes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no input (silent brain) | 1.0 | 0.0 | 15723.27 | 0 |
| LPLC2:L at 150 Hz | 1.0 | 2.845 | 0.35 | 54,236 |
| LPLC2 + LC4, both sides, 150 Hz | 1.0 | 4.165 | 0.24 | 155,306 |

The simulation is event-driven: cost grows with the number of neurons away from rest. With strong visual input it runs slower than real time on this CPU, so the robot loop advances brain time by one frame period per camera frame and reports the ratio.

## Not validated

- Behaviour of a physical robot. No hardware run is recorded in this repository.
- Biological accuracy of the dynamics. Leaky integrate-and-fire neurons with one weight per synapse, predicted transmitters and no gap junctions, neuromodulation, plasticity or graded potentials are a connectome-constrained approximation.
- The camera feature encoders. They are optical-flow heuristics tested on synthetic scenes; webcams, real lighting and motion blur are untested.
